prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a wide, polished educational illustration for an introductory optimization notebook. Soft watercolor and colored-pencil shading on an almost white paper background, clean navy English lettering, gentle blue clock hardware, subtle warm wooden desk, generous whitespace. Match the feel of a friendly university illustrated textbook, not a dashboard. Landscape 3:2. Title: 'One setting, four readings'. Three large groups connected clearly left to right: (1) a blue classroom digital clock beside four observation cards headed 'Recorded errors (min)' with exactly '-2', '-1', '-1', '0'; (2) a physical blue adjustment dial headed 'Choose a correction' with a large '+1 min' label; (3) four result cards headed 'Remaining errors (min)' with exactly '-1', '0', '0', '+1'. A short arrow from the result cards leads downward to a small paper scorecard reading 'Squared-error score' and '1 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 2 min²'. Clock face can simply read 09:59 without assigning that one face to every observation. Make the four observation cards and four result cards clearly separate readings, not four independent controls. The ONE chosen correction applies to ALL four readings. Use blue for the decision dial, navy for text, muted orange to accent this candidate's correction. Avoid extra numbers, people, formulas, logos or complicated backgrounds. All specified text must be correctly spelled, large and readable at 800 px display width. Do not add text other than the specified labels and numeric cards.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a clear conceptual illustration for an introductory calculus and optimization notebook. Wide landscape 3:2, almost-white paper background, refined watercolor and colored-pencil accents, dark navy large clean English typography, simple hand-illustrated scientific textbook style. Main title: 'A flat slope needs a check'. Two equally sized panels with enormous whitespace, like two smooth painted blue ribbons viewed exactly from the side. Left panel is a U-shaped upward-opening curve with a single orange dot EXACTLY at its lowest point; right panel is an inverted U-shaped curve with a single orange dot EXACTLY at its highest point. Each orange dot has a clearly horizontal navy dashed tangent segment centered on it. No axes or tick values: these are conceptual profiles. Labels above the two panels: 'Minimum' and 'Maximum'. Labels below the left panel: 'Nearby values are higher'. Labels below the right panel: 'Nearby values are lower'. At bottom, one shared large sentence: 'Both have zero slope here.' The left curve must rise on BOTH sides of the dot. The right curve must fall on BOTH sides of the dot. Make the shared zero-slope feature obvious, while their neighborhood shapes differ. Do not use mountains, roads, a ball, a 3-D surface, extra extrema or arrows that imply an algorithm. Only one dot and one horizontal tangent in each panel. No extra prose, formulas, watermarks or decorative objects. All lettering legible at an 800 px display width.

Use case: scientific-educational. Create a friendly wide instructional illustration showing the difference between a constant clock correction and a correction that changes with elapsed time. Almost-white paper, soft watercolor and colored-pencil blue clock-control hardware, dark navy large English text, subtle gray guide lines. Landscape 3:2, polished university textbook style. Main title: 'Two settings change the correction'. At top draw a small blue control panel with TWO separate physical knobs labeled 'Initial correction q' and 'Correction per hour r'. Below, compare two clearly aligned horizontal rows of four correction cards. Shared four column headings: '0 h', '1 h', '2 h', '3 h', evenly spaced in chronological order. First row label: 'q = 1 min, r = 0'. Its four cards must read exactly '+1 min', '+1 min', '+1 min', '+1 min'. Second row label: 'q = 1 min, r = −0.1 min/h'. Its four cards must read exactly '+1 min', '+0.9 min', '+0.8 min', '+0.7 min'. Highlight only the changed rate setting with muted orange; the initial correction remains blue and unchanged. Simple flat blue marker heights may support the top row and a gently falling sequence the bottom row, but no additional numeric axes or invented clock times. Footer: 'These are corrections added to the recorded errors.' Teach that q stays fixed while changing r alters later corrections progressively. Exactly two comparison rows, four times, eight cards. The card values are corrections, not remaining errors. No advanced mathematics, gradients, extra data, logos, clutter or other text. Keep all labels large and readable at 800 px display width.

prompt: Use case: scientific-educational. Create a simple beautiful educational illustration explaining why opposite clock errors can cancel in a sum but remain in a squared-error score. Wide landscape 3:2, white paper background, restrained watercolor texture, colored-pencil object shading, dark navy clean English typography, blue observations and orange emphasis. Main title: 'Zero total can hide errors'. Across the top place FOUR equal small clock-error cards, titled collectively 'Remaining errors (min)', showing EXACTLY '−1', '0', '0', '+1'. Under them make TWO clearly separated panels. LEFT panel title: 'Add the signed errors'. Draw a minus-one token and a plus-one token gently canceling visually, with exact large equation '−1 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 0 min'. RIGHT panel title: 'Square, then add'. Show a row of FOUR slots: a filled one-unit blue square under the −1 error, a small gray zero marker for each of the two zero errors, then a filled one-unit blue square under the +1 error. The two nonzero squares are equal in area. Label the four contributions exactly '1', '0', '0', '1'. Beneath this row place the large exact equation '1 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 2 min²'. Bottom line: 'The first and last readings are still wrong.' Make this an illustrated mathematical explanation, not a dense table. No error signs lost in the first sum, no minus sign in squared contributions, no extra clock times, formulas, labels, axes, legends, branding or watermark. All labels readable at 800 px display width.

Keep the four cards, their blue shading, the heading Remaining errors (min), all other panels, tokens, squares, equations, colors and exact wording unchanged. No clock faces, hands or times anywhere. Preserve the two equal filled square tiles and the two zero markers.
